deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§26-27 of E477). The notation is fixed throughout for one 'order' m+n. Euler writes p^μ for the product ζ(μ)ζ(m+n−μ), so that p^μ = p^{m+n−μ}, and p^{m+n} for ζ(m+n) alone. He writes q^μ for the non-strict double sum ∫(1/z^μ)(1/y^{m+n−μ}) = Σ_z z^{−μ} Σ_{y≤z} y^{−(m+n−μ)}, which is ζ*(μ, m+n−μ) in modern notation. The 'first method' (the harmonic, or stuffle, product) gives q^μ + q^{m+n−μ} = p^μ + p^{m+n}; equivalently p^μ = q^μ + q^{m+n−μ} − p^{m+n}.

The series studied is the strict double sum S = Σ_z z^{−n} Σ_{x<z} x^{−m} = q^n − p^{m+n}. Writing z = x + a with x, a ≥ 1 gives S = Σ_{a,x} 1/(x^m (x+a)^n). Euler uses the partial fraction decomposition of §6:
1/(x^m(x+a)^n) = Σ_{k=0}^{m−1} (−1)^k C(n+k−1,k) a^{−(n+k)} x^{−(m−k)} + (−1)^m Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} C(m+k−1,k) a^{−(m+k)} (x+a)^{−(n−k)}.

On this page each piece is summed over all a and x.
- Upper part: Σ a^{−(n+k)} x^{−(m−k)} = ζ(n+k)ζ(m−k) = p^{n+k} = p^{m−k}.
- Lower part: with z = x + a > a, Σ_a a^{−(m+k)} Σ_{z>a} z^{−(n−k)} = ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) − Σ_a a^{−(m+k)} Σ_{z≤a} z^{−(n−k)} = p^{m+k} − q^{m+k}. By the stuffle relation this equals q^{n−k} − p^{m+n}.

Hence
q^n − p^{m+n} = Σ_k (−1)^k C(n+k−1,k) p^{m−k} + (−1)^m Σ_k C(m+k−1,k)(q^{n−k} − p^{m+n}).

Replacing each p^{m−k} by q^{m−k} + q^{n+k} − p^{m+n} and cancelling q^n − p^{m+n} from both sides gives the printed linear relation:
0 = q^m − n(q^{m−1} + q^{n+1}) + C(n+1,2)(q^{m−2} + q^{n+2}) − … + [n − C(n+1,2) + …] p^{m+n} ± Σ C(m+k−1,k) q^{n−k} ∓ Σ C(m+k−1,k) p^{m+n}.

In modern terms this is the partial-fraction ('shuffle') relation combined with the stuffle relation, i.e. the double shuffle relations for depth-2 Euler sums. Its purpose is the subsequent case analysis (next page: m = 1, 2, 3, …). For example, m = 1 gives the depth-2 sum formula Σ_{j=2}^{n} ζ*(j, n+1−j) = n ζ(n+1), and in general it yields the reduction of ζ(a,b) with a+b odd to products of zeta values.

When an exponent equals 1, the separate terms (ζ(1)ζ(·), q^1) diverge. Euler manipulates them formally with the stuffle relation, and the divergent pieces cancel in the final relations.
errors: Third line of the 'inferior part': the printed result '= p^{n−2} − p^{m+n}' is a misprint for '= q^{n−2} − p^{m+n}', by the pattern of the two preceding lines and by the stuffle relation.

Gap (not an error in the outcome): for exponent 1 the individual sums Σ1/x, Σ1/(x+a), p^1 = ζ(1)ζ(m+n−1) and q^1 diverge. Euler treats them formally via the stuffle identity; the divergences cancel (the 1/x − 1/(x+a) terms telescope to harmonic numbers), so the final relations are correct, but this is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Summing the partial fraction decomposition of 1/(x^m(x+a)^n) over all x, a to express a double zeta value through products ζ(i)ζ(j) and other double sums
ideas.modern_name: Shuffle (partial-fraction) relation for double zeta values; with stuffle, the double shuffle relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477) as origin; modern formalization Hoffman, Ihara–Kaneko–Zagier, Gangl–Kaneko–Zagier
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); also in Opera omnia I.15

ideas.what: Relation p^μ = q^μ + q^{m+n−μ} − p^{m+n} between products of zeta values and non-strict double sums
ideas.modern_name: Harmonic (stuffle) product ζ(a)ζ(b) = ζ*(a,b) + ζ*(b,a) − ζ(a+b)

ideas.what: Formal use of divergent symbols with exponent 1 kept consistent with the stuffle relation so that divergences cancel
ideas.modern_name: Stuffle regularization of divergent multiple zeta values

missed.claim: Euler's handling of exponent-1 terms amounts to a consistent formal (stuffle-type) regularization of divergent double zeta symbols, a precursor of the modern regularized double shuffle. The general relation on this page is the combined shuffle+stuffle system. This is broadly recognized in the MZV literature, but the regularization aspect is rarely spelled out.
missed.quote: p^{m}−q^{m}=q^{n}−p^{m+n} ... Cum autem sit p^{μ}=q^{μ}+q^{m+n−μ}−p^{m+n}, habebimus 0=q^{m}−n(q^{m−1}+q^{n+1})+...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution of regularized double shuffle; mainly of historiographic interest since the relations themselves are well known.

deep.surprise_reason: E477 is the well-known origin of double zeta values, the sum formula and the double shuffle idea. This page is a standard step of that derivation; only the implicit formal regularization of divergent terms is mildly noteworthy.
transcription_corrections: Transcription faithfully reproduces the printed misprint '=p^{n-2}-p^{m+n}' in the third inferior-part line; mathematically it should read q^{n-2}-p^{m+n}.
On the next page, 'q^{μ} + q^{n+1-μ} = p^{μ} + p^{n-1}' should be p^{n+1} (order n+1).
